g.text: ftruncate(fd, 20 GiB), then one byte written at 10 GiB.
The size is a number stored with the file, and ftruncate() only changes the number.
Blocks are given to the file when something is written to them. A part that was never written is a hole:
it reads as zeros and takes no space. ls -l shows the size; ls -s and du show the space.
